name: Ama Ata Aidoo
shortBio: Ghanaian feminist philosopher, playwright, and essayist who inverted the colonial anthropological gaze to critique neocolonial alienation, elite mimicry, and African women’s erasure.
centralQuestion: What happens to postcolonial African self-knowledge when educated elites internalize Europe’s contempt for African languages and women?

keyWorks.title: Our Sister Killjoy: or Reflections from a Black-eyed Squint
keyWorks.description: Experimental philosophical-literary critique reversing the European travelogue to interrogate Western modernity and postcolonial brain drain.

keyWorks.title: Changes: A Love Story
keyWorks.description: Explores modern African womanhood, autonomy, and the tensions between inherited marriage norms and professional agency.
